$comment: The single source of truth for watchdog diagnostic texts, shared by the compiler plugin and
the documentation website.
Consumers:
- :compiler-plugin generates WatchdogDiagnosticMessages from this file (see its
build.gradle.kts). The generator appends a final 'See more: <docsBaseUrl><docs>' section
to every message, after messageTrailer if present, and escapes ' as '' for messages with
parameters, which the compiler renders through java.text.MessageFormat.
- docs/plugins/diagnostics.mjs validates the '// !diag[/range/] DIAGNOSTIC_NAME [params]'
Code Hike annotations in docs samples; the docs Code component renders their underlines,
fills the message template parameters, and shows the resulting diagnostic tooltips.
Fields:
name    - the diagnostic name, matching the property in WatchdogDiagnostics.
title   - the H1 of the check page, shown in the docs tooltip.
docs    - the check page path under docsBaseUrl, without an extension.
message - the message template. Docs render it as Markdown; the compiler uses the same text.
Enclose every code reference in backticks.
Write ' as a single quote: the generator escapes it where MessageFormat needs it.
Do not spell out the documentation link; the generator derives it from docs.
messageTrailer - optional sentence appended to the message before the documentation link.
parameterValues - optional named values for long or reusable diagnostic parameters. Values
may have {0}, {1}, ... placeholders. Compiler checkers resolve them through
generated code; docs annotations use $name or $name(value) references.

diagnostics.name: OPEN_API_WITHOUT_SUBCLASS_OPT_IN
diagnostics.title: Open API without subclass opt-in
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` can be subclassed outside the library without restriction, which makes it hard to evolve. Mark it with `@SubclassOptInRequired` to control external subclassing, or with `@IntentionallyOpen` if unrestricted subclassing is intended.

diagnostics.name: SUBCLASS_OPT_IN_WITHOUT_MARKERS
diagnostics.title: Subclass opt-in without markers
diagnostics.message: `@SubclassOptInRequired` lists no marker classes, so it doesn't restrict external subclassing. Pass at least one opt-in marker class with a description of why the subclassing is restricted.

diagnostics.name: EXHAUSTIVE_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Exhaustive public API
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` can be matched exhaustively by users, so adding {2} later is a breaking change. Mark it with `@IntentionallyExhaustive` if this exhaustive shape is an intended part of the API.

diagnostics.name: UNDOCUMENTED_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Undocumented public API
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` is part of the public API but has no `KDoc`. Document it so users don't have to guess its purpose and usage contract, or mark it with `@IntentionallyUndocumented` if leaving it undocumented is intended.

diagnostics.name: FUNCTION_TYPE_ALIAS_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Function type aliases in public API
diagnostics.message: The type alias `{0}` abbreviates a function type, so users bind to the bare function shape: the alias is erased from the compiled API and can't evolve into a richer abstraction later. Declare a `fun interface` instead to keep lambda ergonomics behind a stable nominal type, or mark the alias with `@IntentionallyFunctionTypeAlias` if exposing the function type is intended.

diagnostics.name: DATA_CLASS_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Data classes in public API
diagnostics.message: The `data class` `{0}` bakes its constructor property list into the compiled API through the generated `copy` and `componentN` functions and the constructor itself, so adding, removing, or reordering a property later is a breaking change. Declare a regular class and implement `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString` explicitly, or mark the class with `@IntentionallyDataClass` if this property list is an intended, stable part of the API.

diagnostics.name: STATEFUL_CLASS_WITHOUT_EQUALS
diagnostics.title: Stateful classes without equals
diagnostics.message: The class `{0}` holds state - at least one property with a backing field - but neither declares nor inherits an `equals` implementation, so comparisons use object identity instead of the class's meaningful state. Override `equals` and `hashCode` together. {1} Alternatively, in IntelliJ IDEA press `{2}` or choose `Code | Generate` to generate the methods. Mark the class with `@IntentionallyWithoutEquals` if identity equality is intended, or `@IntentionallyWithoutEqualsHashCodeOrToString` to acknowledge all three inherited implementations.

diagnostics.name: STATEFUL_CLASS_WITHOUT_HASH_CODE
diagnostics.title: Stateful classes without hashCode
diagnostics.message: The class `{0}` holds state - at least one property with a backing field - but neither declares nor inherits a `hashCode` implementation, so hash-based collections use object identity instead of the class's meaningful state. Override `equals` and `hashCode` together. {1} Alternatively, in IntelliJ IDEA press `{2}` or choose `Code | Generate` to generate the methods. Mark the class with `@IntentionallyWithoutHashCode` if identity hashing is intended, or `@IntentionallyWithoutEqualsHashCodeOrToString` to acknowledge all three inherited implementations.

diagnostics.name: STATEFUL_CLASS_WITHOUT_TO_STRING
diagnostics.title: Stateful classes without toString
diagnostics.message: The class `{0}` holds state - at least one property with a backing field - but neither declares nor inherits a `toString` implementation, so instances render as the opaque class-name-with-hash-code default and reveal nothing in logs and debugger output. Override `toString` to render the current state. {1} Alternatively, in IntelliJ IDEA press `{2}` or choose `Code | Generate` to generate the methods. Mark the class with `@IntentionallyWithoutToString` if the opaque rendering is intended, or `@IntentionallyWithoutEqualsHashCodeOrToString` to acknowledge all three inherited implementations.

diagnostics.name: MUTABLE_COLLECTION_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Mutable collections in public API
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` exposes the mutable collection type `{2}`. Once a mutable collection is shared across the API boundary, it is unclear whether user-side and library-side mutations affect each other, and the library can no longer evolve its internal representation freely. Accept and return read-only types instead (arrays count as mutable collections too), handing out defensive copies where needed, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyMutableCollection` if sharing the collection is intended.

diagnostics.name: PAIR_OR_TRIPLE_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Pair and Triple in public API
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` exposes the tuple type `{2}`. Tuple components carry no domain meaning: at the use site `first`/`second`/`third` and positional destructuring reveal nothing about the values, and the fixed shape can't evolve - adding a value means switching to a different type, breaking users. Declare a small class with descriptively named properties instead, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyPairOrTriple` if exposing the tuple is intended.

diagnostics.name: REQUIRED_PARAMETER_AFTER_OPTIONAL
diagnostics.title: Required parameters after optional ones
diagnostics.message: The parameter `{0}` of `{1}` is required but declared after an optional parameter, so it can't be passed positionally without re-stating the defaults in front of it. Declare parameters from the general to the specific: essential inputs first, optional inputs - defaulted and `vararg` parameters - last. Move the required parameter in front of the optional ones, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyRequiredParameterAfterOptional` if this order is intended.

diagnostics.name: INCONSISTENT_PARAMETER_ORDER_IN_OVERLOADS
diagnostics.title: Inconsistent parameter order in overloads
diagnostics.message: The parameters `{0}` and `{1}` of `{2}` appear in the opposite order in another overload. Users transfer their expectations between overloads, so an inconsistent order of same-named parameters invites silently swapped arguments. Keep shared parameters in the same relative order across overloads, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyInconsistentParameterOrder` if the differing order is intended.

diagnostics.name: BOOLEAN_PARAMETER_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Boolean parameters in public API
diagnostics.message: The function `{0}` takes the `Boolean` parameter `{1}`. At the call site a bare `true`/`false` reveals nothing about its meaning, and users can't be forced to name the argument they pass. Introduce separate, descriptively named functions for each mode, or replace the parameter with an `enum class`, or mark it with `@IntentionallyBooleanParameter` if the `Boolean` parameter is intended.

diagnostics.name: NULLABLE_BOOLEAN_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Nullable Booleans in public API
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` exposes a nullable `Boolean`. `Boolean?` models three states but names only two of them, so every use site has to know what `null` stands for, and three-state logic hides in two-branch `if`s. Replace it with an `enum class` naming all three states, or drop the third state, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyNullableBoolean` if the nullable `Boolean` is intended.

diagnostics.name: INLINE_FUNCTION_WITH_LOGIC
diagnostics.title: Inline functions with logic
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` does more than delegate to a function without the `inline` modifier. The compiler copies an `inline` body into every user binary, so logic placed there - and its bugs - stays frozen in users compiled against an old library version until they recompile. Extract the logic into a function without the `inline` modifier (`@PublishedApi internal` if it should stay out of the public API) and delegate to it, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyInlinedLogic` if inlining the logic is intended.

diagnostics.name: MANGLED_JVM_NAME_PUBLIC_API
diagnostics.title: Mangled JVM names in public API
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` has the `value class` `{2}` in its signature, so its compiled JVM name is mangled - or, for a constructor, hidden behind a synthetic one - and Java sources can't call it. Kotlin users are unaffected. Give the compiled code a Java-callable shape with `@JvmName` (`@get:JvmName`/`@set:JvmName` on property accessors) or with `@JvmExposeBoxed`, or mark the declaration with `@IntentionallyMangledJvmName` if Java callers are not supported.

diagnostics.name: KOTLIN_ONLY_API_WITHOUT_JVM_SYNTHETIC
diagnostics.title: Kotlin-only API without JvmSynthetic

parameterValues.suspend: is a `suspend` function, which Java sees with a trailing `Continuation` parameter it can't provide idiomatically
parameterValues.reified: declares a `reified` type parameter, which only inlining Kotlin call sites can substitute - calling the compiled method from Java fails at runtime
parameterValues.suspendFunctionType: takes a `suspend` function type in the parameter `{0}`, which no Java lambda can implement
parameterValues.extensionFunctionType: takes a function type with receiver in the parameter `{0}`, which a Java lambda can only emulate by taking the receiver as an explicit first argument
parameterValues.unitFunctionType: takes a `Unit`-returning function type in the parameter `{0}`, which forces a Java lambda to return the `Unit.INSTANCE` token explicitly

diagnostics.message: The function `{0}` {1}. Kotlin callers see the intended shape, but the function still lands in the API surface Java sources see. Hide the Kotlin-only shape from Java with `@JvmSynthetic`, or provide a Java-friendly alternative alongside - a blocking or `CompletableFuture`-returning bridge for a `suspend` function, a `fun interface` parameter in place of a Kotlin function type - or mark the function with `@IntentionallyKotlinOnlyApi` if leaving the shape visible to Java is intended.

diagnostics.name: COMPANION_API_WITHOUT_JVM_STATIC
diagnostics.title: Companion API without JvmStatic
diagnostics.message: The `companion object` function `{1}` compiles to an instance method on the nested `Companion` class, so Java callers have to reach it as `{0}.Companion.{1}(...)`. Mark it with `@JvmStatic` to additionally compile a static `{0}.{1}(...)` entry point for Java callers - Kotlin call sites are unaffected - or hide it from Java with `@JvmSynthetic`, or mark it with `@IntentionallyNonStaticCompanionApi` if the companion-instance access path is intended.

diagnostics.name: COMPANION_CONSTANT_WITHOUT_JVM_FIELD
diagnostics.title: Companion constants without JvmField
diagnostics.message: The `companion object` property `{1}` compiles to an instance getter on the nested `Companion` class, so Java callers have to read it through `{0}.Companion`. Expose the value on `{0}` itself: as a static field with `@JvmField`, as a compile-time constant with `const val` (primitives and strings), or as a static getter with `@JvmStatic` - or hide the property from Java with `@get:JvmSynthetic`, or mark it with `@IntentionallyNonStaticCompanionApi` if the companion-instance access path is intended.

diagnostics.name: TOP_LEVEL_API_WITHOUT_JVM_NAME
diagnostics.title: Top-level API without JvmName
diagnostics.message: This file's public top-level functions and properties compile into the facade class `{0}`, a name derived from the file name: it reads as an implementation detail at Java call sites, and renaming the file - invisible to Kotlin callers - renames the facade and breaks Java callers. Choose and pin the facade name deliberately with `@file:JvmName`, or mark the file with `@file:IntentionallyDefaultFacadeName` if the derived name is intended.
diagnostics.messageTrailer: Reported once per file, on its first public top-level function or property.

diagnostics.name: DEFAULT_PARAMETERS_WITHOUT_JVM_OVERLOADS
diagnostics.title: Default parameters without JvmOverloads
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` declares default parameter values, but for Java callers the defaults don't exist: only the full signature is compiled, and every argument must be spelled out. Mark the {0} with `@JvmOverloads` to also compile the overloads that let Java callers omit defaulted parameters - trailing ones only: a defaulted parameter in the middle of the list still can't be skipped from Java, and adding a parameter later stays binary incompatible either way - or mark the {0} with `@IntentionallyWithoutJvmOverloads` if serving Java callers the full signature only is intended.

diagnostics.name: PUBLIC_TYPE_FROM_NON_TRANSITIVE_DEPENDENCY
diagnostics.title: Public types from non-transitive dependencies
diagnostics.message: The {0} `{1}` publicly exposes `{2}`, but the dependency providing that type is not published transitively to consumers. Declare the dependency with `api` instead of `implementation`.

diagnostics.name: EXEMPTION_WITHOUT_EXPLANATION
diagnostics.title: Exemptions without explanation
diagnostics.message: The `@{0}` exemption doesn't explain why it is applied: the `{1}` reason doesn't speak for itself, and the `description` is empty. Pass a self-explanatory reason (`FOR_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBILITY`, `API_DESIGN`), or describe the motivation in the `description` argument.

diagnostics.name: DSL_MARKER_NOOP_TARGET
diagnostics.title: DSL markers with no-op targets
diagnostics.message: The DSL marker `{0}` allows the `{1}` annotation target, but a DSL marker only takes effect on classifier declarations (`CLASS`, `ANNOTATION_CLASS`), type usages (`TYPE`), and type aliases (`TYPEALIAS`). Applied to a `{1}` element the marker restricts nothing and only gives a false sense of receiver scope control. Remove the target from `@Target`, or mark the marker with `@IntentionallyWrongDslMarkerTargetsForBackwardsCompatibility` if the target must stay for compatibility with existing users.

diagnostics.name: DSL_MARKER_WITHOUT_EXPLICIT_TARGETS
diagnostics.title: DSL markers without explicit targets
diagnostics.message: The DSL marker `{0}` declares no explicit `@Target`, so it defaults to targets like functions and properties where a DSL marker has no effect, while the effective type usage (`TYPE`) and type alias (`TYPEALIAS`) targets stay unavailable. Declare `@Target(CLASS, TYPE, TYPEALIAS)` or a subset of it, or mark the marker with `@IntentionallyWrongDslMarkerTargetsForBackwardsCompatibility` if the default targets must stay for compatibility with existing users.

diagnostics.name: DSL_MARKER_NOOP_TYPE_POSITION
diagnostics.title: DSL markers on no-op type positions
diagnostics.message: The DSL marker `{0}` has no effect on this {1}: scope control only reacts to markers on the type of an implicit value - a receiver type, a context parameter type, or a function type with such implicit values. A named value is always accessed explicitly, so the marker restricts nothing here. Move it to the class or to a receiver position, or remove it.
